title: ZnS/MgF2 Single-Cavity Defect-Engineered Dual-Band Filter
scientific_hypothesis: A single-cavity structure with carefully engineered defect layers in the Bragg mirror can produce two transmission peaks without requiring two separate cavities, reducing total layer count while maintaining dual-band performance.
design_principle: Introducing controlled defects (thickness variations) within a Bragg mirror creates localized states that produce transmission peaks within the stopband. Two defects at different positions can create two peaks. This topology uses fewer layers than dual-cavity but requires more precise thickness control. L28 discusses Bragg pair constraints for complex filter design.
proposed_topology: Air | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 (defect 1) | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS (defect 2) | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | MgF2 | ZnS | Daimon-20 substrate. Total 20 coating layers.
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 20 coating layers
Defect layer thicknesses for dual-peak positioning
Bragg pair thicknesses for stopband width control
manufacturing_considerations: Fewer layers may reduce stress and deposition time
Defect thickness tolerance may be tighter than dual-cavity approach
theory_basis: Defect mode theory in photonic bandgap structures
Single-cavity with multiple defect states for multi-peak transmission
Global optimization for non-convex thin-film design per L22
expected_advantages: Fewer total layers (20 vs 22) reduces stress and cost
Single-cavity may have simpler optimization landscape
Defect engineering offers finer control over peak positions
known_risks: Two peaks from single cavity may be harder to separate than dual-cavity
Defect positions sensitive to thickness errors
May produce unwanted transmission between the two target bands
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer dielectric multilayer coating on CaF2 (Daimon-20) substrate with air incidence. Stack sequence from air side: MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2 (defect 1), ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS (defect 2), MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, MgF2, ZnS, terminating on CaF2 (Daimon-20). All 20 layer thicknesses are optimizable variables. Wavelength range 2500-5000 nm. Target high transmittance at 3250-3350 nm and 4200-4300 nm. Target low transmittance at 2500-3100 nm and 4450-5000 nm. No metal layers. Unpolarized light at 0 degree incidence.
revision_reason: Repaired CaF2 material name to Daimon-20 per registry resolution requirement
